source.title: Context-based Virtual Adversarial Training for Text Classification with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Do-Myoung Lee; Yeachan Kim; Chang Gyun Seo

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training and test accuracy while training text classifiers with corrupted labels; its analysis reports that the baseline CNN's test accuracy drops as training continues, while ConVAT resists overfitting.
record.gate_note: The paper studies text classification with noisy labels, not the claim's image setting or completely random labeling. Its main table reports test accuracy, not training error. Figure 3 plots train, validation and test accuracy over training epochs at 50% uniform noise; no exact values are stated for that figure.
record.test_reason: The baseline CNN experiments provide qualitative evidence of learning useful class structure before later memorizing label noise in text classification (V6). Table 1 also tests the test-performance component of V4. The study does not establish perfect training fit across noise rates.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that ConVAT resists overfitting to noisy labels and performs well in their text-classification experiments. This does not establish prevention of memorization under completely random labeling.
record.recipe_differences: Text classification with synthetic uniform or random label noise, using a CNN backbone and context-based adversarial training; not the original image-classification random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and noise type and rate vary in the reported test-accuracy table. Figure 3 analyzes training over epochs on three datasets at 50% uniform noise.

fits_no_version.finding: ConVAT maintains test performance during training better than the baseline CNN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Context-level virtual adversarial training mitigates overfitting under synthetic label noise in text classification.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
record.problems: Training-accuracy values in Figure 3 are not stated in the text; the analysis covers three datasets at one noise rate and type. The paper's main table reports test accuracy rather than training error.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Table 1's test-accuracy values across methods, datasets and noise rates do not report the training-fit measure required by V4; Figure 3 is the paper's direct training-curve analysis relevant to that version.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling fitted to zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Time to fit true versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions. ConVAT-versus-VAT computational cost measures a different comparison.
Perfect training fit at every corruption fraction and the full trajectory through completely random labeling. Early stopping is used for the main results.
The specified weight-decay, dropout and data-augmentation comparisons, including their removal on true labels.
Separate quantitative learning curves for clean and corrupted examples, and completely random-label training.

missing.what: The baseline CNN's TREC context vectors initially show class clusters and subsequently lose them, providing additional qualitative evidence for V6.
missing.locator: Section 5.1, Figure 6(b), TREC with 50% uniform noise

record.verdict_notes: Table 1's baseline CNN test accuracy decreases monotonically across the reported uniform-noise rates, supporting V4's test-degradation component. Those results are explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing; no V4 verdict is assigned without linked result rows. The supplied text contains no readable numerical Figure 3 curves. The introduction's nearly 100% training-accuracy statement cites prior work and is not this study's result. Neither text classification nor externally corrupted training labels alone disqualifies a test.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, unchanged original architecture and hyperparameters, and generalization on true labels.
Training time to fit true versus random labels and convergence time as corruption increases.

The paper plots training accuracy under 50% uniform noise but does not state that training fit is perfect. The text does not report a steadily rising test error across corruption rates while training fit remains perfect.
Weight decay, dropout and data augmentation under random labels, and their removal under true labels.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, or whether real and random labels are learned differently over training.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on TREC with 50% of training samples corrupted by uniform noise; train, validation and test accuracy plotted by epoch.
rows.measure: Training, validation and test accuracy over training epochs
rows.note: The authors state that CNN train accuracy tends to keep increasing while test accuracy drops after certain points; exact values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Section 5.1 describes increasing training accuracy followed by declining test accuracy attributed to memorization. This bears on learning dynamics, not degradation across corruption rates. Exact training accuracy is unavailable.

rows.subject: ConVAT
rows.operation_detail: Trained on TREC with 50% of training samples corrupted by uniform noise; train, validation and test accuracy plotted by epoch.
rows.measure: Training, validation and test accuracy over training epochs
rows.note: The authors state that ConVAT maintains performance robustly and increases little by little; exact values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: This is the proposed mitigation method's performance comparison. Maintained test accuracy does not establish perfect noisy-label fit, degradation across corruption rates, or the order of learning clean and noisy labels.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on SST with 50% of training samples corrupted by uniform noise; train, validation and test accuracy plotted by epoch.
rows.measure: Training, validation and test accuracy over training epochs
rows.note: The authors describe the same trend across the analyzed datasets: CNN train accuracy increases and test accuracy drops after a point.
rows.check: The authors describe useful early generalization followed by increasing training accuracy and declining test accuracy attributed to memorization. A single corruption rate cannot establish V4's across-rate trajectory.

rows.subject: ConVAT
rows.operation_detail: Trained on SST with 50% of training samples corrupted by uniform noise; train, validation and test accuracy plotted by epoch.
rows.measure: Training, validation and test accuracy over training epochs
rows.note: The authors describe ConVAT as maintaining performance robustly and increasing little by little; exact values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: This proposed-method comparison reports resistance to overfitting, without establishing any version's specified effect.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Ag-News with 50% of training samples corrupted by uniform noise; train, validation and test accuracy plotted by epoch.
rows.measure: Training, validation and test accuracy over training epochs
rows.note: The authors describe the same trend across the analyzed datasets: CNN train accuracy increases and test accuracy drops after a point.
rows.check: The reported temporal pattern supports later noise memorization after useful learning. It does not measure degradation as the corruption fraction changes.

rows.subject: ConVAT
rows.operation_detail: Trained on Ag-News with 50% of training samples corrupted by uniform noise; train, validation and test accuracy plotted by epoch.
rows.measure: Training, validation and test accuracy over training epochs
rows.note: The authors describe ConVAT as maintaining performance robustly and increasing little by little; exact values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: This proposed-method comparison reports resistance to overfitting, without measuring clean-versus-noisy learning order or V4's across-rate trajectory.

relationships.condition: Baseline CNN on TREC, SST and AG-News with 50% uniform label noise.
relationships.reason: R1, R3 and R5 describe training accuracy continuing upward after test performance deteriorates; Section 5.1 attributes the later deterioration to memorization. This is qualitative evidence of useful learning preceding noise memorization.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy continued rising after test performance deteriorated, with the authors attributing the later deterioration to memorization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
